question.problem:
Find $\textrm{E}\big[X^2-3X+3\big],$ given that the continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x) = 2x, \qquad 0 < x < 1.
$$
question.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ and a function $r(x),$ the rule of the lazy statistician states that 

$$
\textrm{E}[r(X)] = \int^{\infty}_{-\infty} r(x)f(x) \: \textrm{d}x.
$$

In our case, we have 

$$
r(X)=x^2-3x+3.
$$

 

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}-3X+3] & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }r(x)f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}({x}^{2}-3x+3)\cdot 2x\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(2{x}^{3}-6{x}^{2}+6x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{{x}^{4}}{2}-2{x}^{3}+3{x}^{2}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =[\frac{1}{2}-2+3]-0 \\  & =\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
